clue.text: Stop first man joining the Mayflower

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark, one of the stops
first abbreviates to 1ST, written here with the figure 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone halts the first passenger trying to board the Pilgrim Fathers' ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'first' piece is the abbreviation 1st, with the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower carried settlers to found a New World plantation, so one aboard was a settler of a new territory.

clue.text: Unpopular adult is left behind

parts.note: something out of favour is out
a grown person is an adult

explanation.surface: A disliked grown-up has been abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outgrown has been passed by as one develops, like childhood clothes or habits.

clue.text: Oilcloth does produce a distinctive accessory

indicators.note: produce means the letters of oilcloth does are worked into something new

explanation.surface: Waxed fabric makes a stylish add-on.
explanation.walkthrough: An old school tie is worn by former pupils of a (usually British public) school as a mark of membership.
explanation.definitionFit: This necktie marks out a school's former pupils, an accessory that identifies its wearer.

clue.text: I'm not disheartened about long hair pervading everywhere

indicators.note: about means the trimmed phrase goes around the long hair
disheartened means the heart, the middle letter, of the phrase is removed

parts.note: a mane is a long growth of hair

explanation.surface: Someone insists they are not downcast about flowing locks spreading all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' drops the O at the centre of IMNOT, leaving IMNT, which goes 'about' MANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanent describes something present throughout, inherent in everything, as God is said to be.

clue.text: Earth is better than sticky fluid

parts.note: to top something is to beat it, so tops means is better than
oil is a viscous liquid

explanation.surface: Soil is superior to a greasy liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsoil is the upper layer of soil, the earth where plants grow.

clue.text: Money for a junket is raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: rennet is the curdling agent used to make junket, a milk pudding

explanation.surface: Cash for a jolly outing has been collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junket' suggests a jolly, but it is the milk pudding set with rennet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is a ten-pound note, British slang for a sum of cash.

clue.text: Did she rage somewhat at her husband's infidelities?

definitions.text: Did she rage somewhat at her husband's infidelities?

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the phrase she rage is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A question whether a wronged wife was a little angry at her spouse's affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth, Zeus's wife was famously jealous of his many lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen of the Greek gods was furious at Zeus's many affairs.

clue.text: Street is getting bigger

explanation.definitionFit: A curved row of houses is often a named road; also, from Latin, growing, as the waxing moon does.

clue.text: Told this is the way to catch

indicators.note: told means spoken aloud, so we want a phrase that sounds the same as one meaning this way

parts.note: someone beckoning says 'over here', pointing the way

explanation.surface: Someone is being instructed in the correct method of catching.
explanation.walkthrough: The call 'Over here!' (this way) sounds like the verb meaning to catch words not meant for you.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark is to hear it, often by accident, as an eavesdropper does.

clue.text: No end of room on this farm

indicators.note: no end of means the last letter of the word for a room is dropped

parts.note: a study is a room for reading and writing

explanation.surface: On this farm the rooms are endless.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a farm where horses are kept for breeding.

clue.text: Once it was standard to put a small light in front of shipping hazards

indicators.note: in front of places the word for a small light before the word for shipping hazards

parts.note: a star is a small light in the night sky
sandbars are ridges of sand that can ground ships

explanation.surface: It used to be normal to place a little lamp ahead of dangers to vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like 'normal' but means a flag: the Stars and Bars was a flag of the Confederacy in the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and this was an early flag of the Confederate States, no longer flown officially.

clue.text: Menial woman got into fight after some drink

indicators.note: after places the menial's second part behind the drink

parts.note: a bottle is a quantity of drink

indicators.note: got into means the woman sits inside the fight

parts.note: a war is a fight
she stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A servant girl started a brawl after a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle-washer is a lowly drudge doing the dullest jobs.

clue.text: She's making a concession — hurry

definitions.note: the clue reads 'She is making', so the name of a woman is what is defined

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or appease
hie is an old word for hasten

explanation.surface: A woman is giving ground, and quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'She's making' as 'she is made from': the name is built from the pieces that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, so it can stand for 'she'.

clue.text: Nettle appears to cause skin reaction

explanation.surface: A stinging plant seems to bring on a rash.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to annoy them; also, to inflame or make the skin itch and redden.

clue.text: Strange Scottish hut, dilapidated and rough

parts.note: unco is the Scots word for strange or unusual

indicators.note: dilapidated suggests a hut fallen into disrepair, so its letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A peculiar, run-down Highland shack is crude.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR read 'but'; the page prints 'hut'. 'dilapidated' turns HUT into UTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncouth behaviour is coarse and lacking manners, as rough behaviour is.

clue.text: A Continental breed sounds as if it's not hunted here

indicators.note: sounds as if means the words are spoken aloud to give something that sounds alike

parts.note: un is French for a, and a sort is a breed or kind

explanation.surface: A European dog breed apparently isn't chased in these parts.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent UN SORT sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsought has not been searched for or pursued.

clue.text: Heavy mass of mineral in explosion

indicators.note: in means the mineral's symbol sits inside the word for an explosion

parts.note: a blast is an explosion
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium, mined as bauxite

explanation.surface: A heavy lump of ore is caught up in a detonation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is heavy material carried low in a ship to keep it steady.

clue.text: The rain fell freely round this modern protagonist

indicators.note: fell freely means the letters of the rain tumble into a new order

parts.note: a round thing, a ring, is the letter O

explanation.surface: Rain pours down around the hero of a contemporary story.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR read 'nain'; the page prints 'rain'. 'fell freely' turns THERAIN into ANTIHER.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central character lacking heroic qualities, typical of modern fiction.

clue.text: Capital pudding out of a tin, perhaps

indicators.note: out of means the pudding sits outside the other part

parts.note: sago is a starchy milk pudding

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of a tin may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Top-notch dessert straight from the can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like an adjective praising the pudding but names a city; 'out of' has the pudding enclosing the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital city of Chile.

clue.text: Measurement of loudness of badly-delivered song is acceptable

parts.note: a bel is a unit for measuring loudness, ten decibels

indicators.note: badly-delivered means the letters of song come out in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Gauging how loud a poorly sung number is proves fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that belongs fits in, is suitable or proper where it is.

clue.text: Together, hold all types of legal proceeding

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a legal action
a case is a matter brought before a court

explanation.surface: Combined, these cover every kind of court action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold all' reads as 'contain everything', but it is the holdall, a travelling bag; 'Together' tells you to join the two legal words.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large bag for travel, much like a case for clothes.

clue.text: Passage said to be of benefit to Noah?

indicators.note: said means the phrase is spoken aloud to give a word that sounds alike

parts.note: Noah built the ark, and help for it would be ark aid

explanation.surface: A corridor is reputed to have helped the builder of the Flood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a covered walkway, often lined with shops.

clue.text: African poet in the army

indicators.note: in means the poet sits inside the abbreviation for the army

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve
Shakespeare is the Swan of Avon, so swan can stand for a poet

explanation.surface: A writer of verse from Africa has joined up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tswana are a people of Botswana and South Africa.

clue.text: Held counters arranged in combinations

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of held counters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Counters gripped are set out in various groupings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combinations' suggests mathematics, but here means the old one-piece undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: Combinations were a one-piece vest and long drawers, a kind of undergarment.

clue.text: There's a style about this picture

indicators.note: about means the word for style goes around the letter A

parts.note: to dub someone is to style or name them

explanation.surface: This painting has a certain flair to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' looks like a noun but is the verb, to name.
explanation.definitionFit: A daub is a crude painting, a poorly made picture.

clue.text: Subject and chief

explanation.definitionFit: A heading or topic of discussion; also the leader or person in charge.

clue.text: Put up with return of guardian

definitions.text: Put up with return of guardian

parts.note: to house someone is to put them up

indicators.note: return of means the word for a guardian deity is read backwards

parts.note: a god can be a protecting or guardian deity

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a protector coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as 'tolerate', but 'Put up' gives HOUSE and 'with' just joins; 'return of' turns GOD into DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog kept in a home is a guard: housing one gives you a protector that turns the deity about.

clue.text: Appear to secure replacement for shop premises

parts.note: to show up is to appear

indicators.note: replacement means the letters of the word for secure are put back in a different order

parts.note: to moor a boat is to secure it

explanation.surface: Turn up to arrange a substitute for the store's premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A showroom is a room where goods are displayed for sale.
